assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength idea with ultracold strontium and ytterbium atoms and has reached fractional uncertainties near 10^-18. It is a clear, original advance in precision atomic physics, with direct consequences for timekeeping, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. As an atomic physicist I find the underlying atomic-structure and light-shift physics convincing.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the first lattice clocks; Ye's group drove the strontium clocks to record accuracy and stability and linked them to optical frequency combs. The two-name credit is clean and supports a fair prize. I rely on recalled history rather than verifying details such as Ye's JILA collaborators.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks in several countries confirm the performance, and the field has been stable for over a decade. Recognition is timely. The 2005 prize covered frequency combs and the 2012 prize covered ion control, but this is a distinct invention.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier AMO prizes could make the committee see this as incremental.
Credit for the 10^-18 milestone also involves other groups (e.g. NIST, PTB, RIKEN) that this two-name list leaves out.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions, together with its experimental realisation and scaling to many-qubit processors and simulators, is a foundational contribution to quantum information. The combination of an original theoretical idea and demanding experiments gives it strong lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive 1995 proposal, and Blatt's group did some of the earliest and most complete demonstrations of gates, entanglement and simulation. Wineland and Haroche were recognised in 2012 for the underlying control of single quantum systems, and other experimental groups (Wineland/NIST, Monroe, Innsbruck, Oxford) also contributed. A three-person split is plausible but not uniquely determined.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation by many independent groups, and commercial machines now exist. Recognition is mature. The remaining question is how it relates to the 2012 prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat this as an extension of the 2012 prize.
Fair credit among the experimental trapped-ion groups is open.
Cirac and Zoller also appear on the optical-lattice candidate, which could create allocation conflicts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect, followed by the HgTe observation of edge transport, opened a large field of topological quantum matter. The idea is original and conceptually clear, and its influence on condensed matter physics has been broad.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction (the graphene proposal and the Z2 classification), and Molenkamp's group did the decisive HgTe experiment together with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang theory. Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators and Zhang's early role are credited elsewhere in the field, so the three-person set is defensible but incomplete. Haldane, Kosterlitz and Thouless were honoured in 2016 for earlier topological ideas.
assessment.maturity: Many independent experiments confirm the effect and the classification is stable. Timing is good, although 2016 already recognised topological phases of matter.
uncertainties: The BHZ theory and 3D topological insulator experiments make the proper credit set contested.
The 2016 prize may reduce the appetite for a second topology prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with controllable parameters, as shown by the superfluid-Mott transition and later quantum gas microscopy. This is a strong, original example of quantum simulation of many-body physics, and it overlaps well with atomic many-body theory.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal supplied the key theory, and the Greiner-Bloch experiment gave the Mott demonstration. Esslinger's fermionic work and the Greiner/Bloch microscopes add further contributions. Five names are credited, so a three-person set requires a choice that leaves out Zoller and Cirac. Allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The field is well confirmed across many labs, but its largest scientific payoff (solving open Hubbard-model questions) is only partly delivered. It is therefore mature enough, but the timing is less clear than for the clock or trapped-ion candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward theory (Zoller, Jaksch) as well as experiment.
Whether quantum simulation has yet answered an open problem convincingly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned the moire flat band prediction into a platform with correlated insulators and superconductivity. The idea is original and the experimental discovery opened an entirely new research direction.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands at the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulators and superconductivity. Other experimental groups (Dean, Yacoby, Young, and others) and theorists (Santos-Peres, Kim) contributed. The three-person set is natural for the discovery and the theory.
assessment.maturity: The effect has been reproduced widely since 2018. It is still a young field, and the interpretation of the superconductivity is not settled, which makes timing arguably premature.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
The field is only about eight years old, and prize caution is likely.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry exploits matter-wave coherence for precision measurement of gravity, rotation and fundamental constants, including tests of the equivalence principle. It builds on laser cooling and the Ramsey method, and it has real scientific and instrumental importance.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard, Bordé and Kasevich all made foundational contributions (Pritchard on early atom interferometers, Bordé on the theory and Ramsey-Bordé interferometry, Kasevich on light-pulse gravimeters and gradiometers). Chu and Cohen-Tannoudji were recognised in 1997 for related laser cooling. Four names are credited, and Schmiedmayer's role is real. Credit is plausible but partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Mature technology with field instruments and long baseline experiments. The strongest results (such as tests of fundamental physics at new levels) are still developing.
uncertainties: Attribution is spread over several pioneers and the clean decisive contributions are debated.
Overlap with the 1997 laser cooling prize and the 2001 BEC prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brings cavity QED to superconducting artificial atoms, with strong coupling, dispersive readout and the transmon design. It underlies modern superconducting quantum processors and extends the Haroche-style physics that I know well from atomic systems.
assessment.attribution: The Blais-Huang-Wallraff-Girvin-Schoelkopf 2004 proposal and the Wallraff et al. strong-coupling demonstration are the key works. The group credit is large (Blais is also named), and a three-person set leaves out one of the theory authors. Yale and ETH Zurich were clearly central.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed and technologically important. However, the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, so recognition of a closely related area soon after is a timing concern.
uncertainties: Allocation among Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff, and relation to transmon and other qubit work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains the flatness and horizon problems and supplies a quantum origin for primordial fluctuations, with predictions that are consistent with CMB measurements. The scientific impact is very large and the Mukhanov calculation of perturbations is a key piece.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed inflation, Linde developed new and chaotic inflation, and Mukhanov computed the fluctuation spectrum. Starobinsky and Albrecht-Steinhardt also have strong claims. The credited set is reasonable but leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Core inflationary predictions are supported by CMB data, but there is no direct evidence of the inflaton or primordial gravitational waves, so the confirmation is indirect. The question of whether recognition is premature remains open. This is outside my own expertise, so my confidence is lower here.
uncertainties: No decisive observational test such as primordial B-modes.
Starobinsky is not in the credited names, which weakens the attribution.
